Used exclusively for $0 dry-runs of the absolute runner. It speaks just enough of the OpenAI shape to let every suite exercise its full code path — routing, timing, tool-call parsing, and file writes — without talking to RunPod. Run with: python mock_openai_server.py --port 8089 Then point the runner at it: python run_absolute_benchmark.py ... --endpoint-override mock The mock's behavior: - Returns a canned assistant message for any user prompt. - When tools are present, returns a tool_call for the first tool, with arguments it tries to infer from the last user message via a tiny keyword parser (enough to make tool_calling_simple pass on {2,3,17,25,...}). - Returns usage tokens by character-count heuristic. - Adds a short artificial delay so timing measurements are non-zero. \"\"\" from __future__ import annotations import argparse import json import re import time import uuid from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer from typing import Any DELAY_SECONDS = 0.05 class MockHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_POST(self) -> None: # noqa: N802 if self.path not in (\"/v1/chat/completions\",): self.send_error(404, f\"no mock for {self.path}\") return length = int(self.headers.get(\"Content-Length\", \"0\")) raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length > 0 else b\"{}\" try: request = json.loads(raw.decode(\"utf-8\")) except json.JSONDecodeError: self.send_error(400, \"invalid JSON\") return time.sleep(DELAY_SECONDS) response = _build_response(request) body = json.dumps(response).encode(\"utf-8\") self.send_response(200) self.send_header(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\") self.send_header(\"Content-Length\", str(len(body))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(body) def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None: # noqa: A002 # Quieter than default; prefix with timestamp-ish import sys sys.stderr.write(\"[mock] \" + (format % args) + \"\n\") def _build_response(request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]: messages = request.get(\"messages\", []) tools = request.get(\"tools\") last_user = _last_user_message(messages) if tools: message = _build_tool_call_response(last_user, tools) else: message = { \"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": _build_text_response(last_user), } # Approximate usage by character count / 4 prompt_chars = sum(len(_stringify(m.get(\"content\", \"\"))) for m in messages) completion_chars = len(_stringify(message.get(\"content\", \"\") or \"\")) return { \"id\": f\"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}\", \"object\": \"chat.completion\", \"created\": int(time.time()), \"model\": request.get(\"model\", \"mock-model\"), \"choices\": [ { \"index\": 0, \"message\": message, \"finish_reason\": \"tool_calls\" if message.get(\"tool_calls\") else \"stop\", } ], \"usage\": { \"prompt_tokens\": max(prompt_chars // 4, 1), \"completion_tokens\": max(completion_chars // 4, 1), \"total_tokens\": max((prompt_chars + completion_chars) // 4, 1), }, } def _build_text_response(last_user: str) -> str: if \"limerick\" in last_user.lower(): return ( \"There once was a language called Python,\n\" \"Whose scripts were a joy to write in.\n\" \"With indents so clean,\n\" \"And imports between,\n\" \"It kept bugs from finding a way in.\" ) if \"haiku\" in last_user.lower(): return \"Type error appears\nValues mismatched in the slot\nStack trace breathes silence\" if \"regex\" in last_user.lower(): return ( \"It matches one or more characters that are commas, semicolons, \" \"or whitespace. Used with re.split(), it splits a string at any \" \"run of those separators.\" ) if \"awake\" in last_user.lower() or \"ready\" in last_user.lower(): return \"Yes, I am awake.\" return \"Mock assistant response.\" _NUM_RE = re.compile(r\"-?\d+\.?\d*\") def _build_tool_call_response(last_user: str, tools: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]: first_tool = tools[0] name = first_tool.get(\"function\", {}).get(\"name\", \"mystery\") nums = [float(m) for m in _NUM_RE.findall(last_user)] # Best-effort argument inference: take first two numbers as a, b args: dict[str, Any] = {} if name in (\"add\", \"subtract\", \"multiply\", \"divide\"): a = nums[0] if len(nums) >= 1 else 0 b = nums[1] if len(nums) >= 2 else 0 args = {\"a\": a, \"b\": b} else: # Generic placeholder: supply dummies for each required param for param_name, param_spec in ( first_tool.get(\"function\", {}).get(\"parameters\", {}).get(\"properties\", {}).items() ): if param_spec.get(\"type\") == \"integer\": args[param_name] = 1 elif param_spec.get(\"type\") == \"number\": args[param_name] = 1.0 else: args[param_name] = \"mock\" return { \"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": None, \"tool_calls\": [ { \"id\": f\"call_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\", \"type\": \"function\", \"function\": { \"name\": name, \"arguments\": json.dumps(args), }, } ], } def _last_user_message(messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str: for msg in reversed(messages): if msg.get(\"role\") == \"user\": return _stringify(msg.get(\"content\", \"\")) return \"\" def _stringify(value: Any) -> str: if isinstance(value, str): return value if isinstance(value, list): # OpenAI multimodal content parts = [] for item in value: if isinstance(item, dict): if item.get(\"type\") == \"text\": parts.append(item.get(\"text\", \"\")) else: parts.append(f\"<{item.get('type', 'unknown')}>\") return \" \".join(parts) return json.dumps(value) def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument(\"--host\", default=\"127.0.0.1\") parser.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8089) args = parser.parse_args() server = ThreadingHTTPServer((args.host, args.port), MockHandler) print(f\"mock server listening on http://{args.host}:{args.port}/v1/chat/completions\") try: server.serve_forever() except KeyboardInterrupt: print(\"shutting down\") server.server_close() if __name__ == \"__main__\": main() " 6db98fe250a0663fc1f3ca970199ae6ac63cd8bc:training/qwen35_0p8b_tool_finetune/data/v6_pilot/claude_code_dedup_all.viewer.html:9615: "command": "sleep 1 && curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8089/v1/chat/completions -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"model\":\"test\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is 2+3? Use the add tool.\"}],\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"function\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"add\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"a\":{\"type\":\"integer\"},\"b\":{\"type\":\"integer\"}},\"required\":[\"a\",\"b\"]}}}]}' | python3 -m json.tool", 6db98fe250a0663fc1f3ca970199ae6ac63cd8bc:training/qwen35_0p8b_tool_finetune/data/v6_pilot/claude_code_dedup_all.viewer.html:11380: "content": "# Benchmarking Open LLMs on RunPod Serverless — Setup Notes & Gotchas > A walkthrough of getting a multi-model, multi-suite benchmark harness running on > RunPod's serverless GPU platform, including the two non-obvious complications > that ate a combined two hours and zero dollars: a Docker Hub rate limit that > only manifests on shared worker IPs, and GPU pool availability that silently > stalls queued requests when your chosen GPU class has no capacity. Both have > clean fixes once you know what you're looking at. **Date**: 2026-04-16 **Platform**: RunPod Serverless (pay-per-second GPU) **Tooling**: RunPod MCP server for endpoint management from Claude Code, Python stdlib benchmark runner speaking RunPod's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, local mock server for $0 validation. --- ## Contents 1. Why RunPod Serverless for benchmarking 2. Part 1 — Installing the RunPod MCP server and wiring it to Claude Code 3. Part 2 — First deploy attempt and the Docker Hub rate-limit trap 4. Part 3 — Adding Docker Hub authentication, with a REST API detour 5. Part 4 — GPU pool availability and multi-GPU fallback 6. Part 5 — The benchmark runner design choices that saved us money 7. Cost audit so far 8. Takeaways and checklist --- ## 1. Why RunPod Serverless for benchmarking Local hardware is fine for 4B models; it stops being fine around 30B and gets comical at 70B. Pay-per-second cloud GPU is a natural fit for *benchmarking* specifically — the workload is bursty (one model at a time, few minutes per suite), there's no continuous traffic to amortize a 24/7 pod against, and idle cost between runs should be zero. RunPod bills serverless workers by the second of active compute. When you set `workersMin=0`, there's no idle charge — the endpoint configuration persists for free, and a worker only spins up when a request arrives. For a 10-model sweep that will total maybe 4 hours of actual GPU time, the expected spend is in the tens of dollars. Set the same thing up on a 24/7 pod and you'd pay for 20 idle hours per billable hour of benchmarking. The flip side, which this article is mostly about: any flow that spins up fresh workers **constantly** is exposed to cold-start failure modes that don't exist on a persistent pod. We hit two of them on day one. --- ## 2. Part 1 — Installing the RunPod MCP server RunPod ships an official Model Context Protocol server (`@runpod/mcp-server`) that exposes their REST API as a set of tools an AI assistant can call. The relevant tools for this workflow: - `create-template` / `update-template` / `delete-template` - `create-endpoint` / `update-endpoint` / `delete-endpoint` - `create-container-registry-auth` - `get-endpoint` (with `includeWorkers: true`) - `list-*` for each resource type Install into Claude Code (user scope so it's available across projects): ```bash claude mcp add runpod --scope user \ -e RUNPOD_API_KEY=your_runpod_api_key_here \ -- npx -y @runpod/mcp-server@latest ``` Restart Claude Code. Run `/mcp` to confirm the `runpod` server shows as connected. Verify with a read-only probe: ``` list-endpoints → [] ``` Important subtlety: the `-e RUNPOD_API_KEY=...` in the install command injects the key **only into the MCP server subprocess's environment**. It is **not** exported to your shell. Anything you run from your terminal or from Claude Code's Bash tool will not see `$RUNPOD_API_KEY` unless you export it separately. For our Python benchmark runner (which talks to RunPod's OpenAI-compatible endpoint directly, not through MCP), we extract the key at ru ... command output truncated for persistence ... a can paste a `request_id` and see the full event tree. Andre can see what Pablo's APK actually did during a test. \"I cant have an agent running wild without being able to retrace his steps\" — solved. **Scope:** 1. New endpoint `GET /v1/observability/runs/{request_id}/replay` returns: ```json { \"request_id\": \"...\", \"tree\": [ {\"event_id\": \"...\", \"kind\": \"chat_received\", \"ts\": \"...\", \"actor\": \"mobile\", \"data\": {...}}, {\"event_id\": \"...\", \"kind\": \"dispatch_decision\", \"ts\": \"...\", \"actor\": \"brain\", \"data\": {\"transport\": \"ws\", \"node\": \"...\"}, \"children\": [...]}, ... ], \"summary\": {\"model\": \"qwen3.5:0.8b\", \"tokens\": {...}, \"duration_ms\": 726, \"outcome\": \"ok\"} } ``` 2. Server-rendered HTML page at `/v1/observability/runs.html`: - Table: recent 100 runs (request_id, ts, model, tokens, outcome). - Click a row → full event tree (collapsible). - Each step shows: ts, actor, event, raw data (folded JSON). 3. Andre to spec the visual hierarchy + interaction (collapse, filter, search). 4. **Optional Phase 5b: replay execution** — RBAC'd to dev mode, re-run a captured prompt against the same model, diff the output. Useful for regression testing model changes. ### Phase 6 — Token-class breakdown for monetization (Atlas, ~3 days) **Goal:** Per-turn tokens decomposed into thinking / tool-call / final-answer. Ratio tracked. Cost computable per model rate. **Scope:** 1. Post-hoc parser in `app/services/token_classifier.py`: - Input: full assistant response text + tool_calls JSON. - Output: `{thinking_tokens, tool_call_tokens, final_answer_tokens}`. - Strategy: regex `<think>...</think>` for thinking; tool_calls array length × per-call token cost for tools; remainder = final. 2. Rerun on chat_done in `_proxy_chat_stream`, persist to `chat_turn_summaries`. 3. New table `model_pricing`: ```sql CREATE TABLE model_pricing ( model TEXT PRIMARY KEY, input_per_1k_usd NUMERIC(10, 6), output_per_1k_usd NUMERIC(10, 6), thinking_per_1k_usd NUMERIC(10, 6), -- often == output rate effective_from TIMESTAMPTZ, effective_to TIMESTAMPTZ ); ``` - Local Ollama models default to 0 (or \"compute_cost_only\"). - OpenAI / Anthropic / Groq populated with public rates. 4. New endpoint `GET /v1/observability/usage?since=<ts>` returns token + cost rollups by model / thread / user / day. 5. Future: add user / org dimension if multi-user comes online. ### Phase 7 — Retention + cold archival (Bane, ~2 days) **Goal:** Long-term storage cost is bounded. >1y events go cold. Hot DB doesn't grow forever. **Scope:** 1. Postgres partitioning: monthly partitions on `chat_turn_summaries`, `telemetry_events`, `prompt_traces`, `tool_calls`, `model_calls`. Drop partitions > 365d. 2. JSONL rotation: daily file, gzip after 7 days, archive to cicd `/var/www/weeyuga-archives/` after 90 days. 3. Ground graph: keeps all events forever (it's our cold layer). 4. Backup: nightly `pg_dump` of recent (30d) partitions to cicd. --- ## Source-of-truth contract (what each layer answers) | Question | Answer source | |---|---| | \"Which model is the app calling RIGHT NOW?\" | brain log + `chat_turn_summaries` last row | | \"How many tokens did Sloba spend today?\" | `GET /v1/observability/usage?since=00:00 UTC` | | \"Replay run abcd1234\" | `GET /v1/observability/runs/abcd1234/replay` | | \"Show me every voice clip that failed transcribe\" | brain DB SQL: `JOIN messages m ON m.attachments`. Or ground graph traversal for older. | | \"Train on every chat I had with qwen2.5:7b\" | export from ground graph (cold), filter by `operation.llm.model` | | \"What did agent X do during run Y\" | `request_id` filter across `chat_turn_summaries` + `tool_calls` + `model_calls` | | \"Which prompts caused the model to spiral into thinking\" | `chat_turn_summaries` filter `thinking_tokens > 100 AND output_tokens < 20` | | \"How much should I charge for 1000 turns\" | `chat_turn_summaries` × `model_pricing` aggregate | --- ## Hard rules 1. **Telemetry never blocks user-facing latency.** Async sink only; fire-and-forget; failure logged not raised. 2. **`request_id` is immutable.** Once generated, never reused, never deleted. The universal trace key. 3. **Ground envelope is the contract.** Don't fork the schema. If we need new fields, propose them upstream to ground. 4. **PII default**: chat content stays in Postgres only. JSONL ledger captures shape (token counts, model, latency, outcome) but NOT raw content unless `WEEYUGA_TELEMETRY_INCLUDE_CONTENT=1` is set. Ground graph can have content for projects opted-in (default off; per-thread or per-user toggle later). 5. **Backwards compatible**: every phase only ADDS columns or tables; never breaks existing readers. Phase-1 mobile path change is purely additive (`meta_json` JSONB key). 6. **No silent data loss**: if the JSONL ledger is unwritable, log loud and refuse the chat (or buffer to memory + retry); DON'T silently drop events. 7. **Timestamps are RFC3339 UTC**, server-side. Don't trust client clocks for ordering; use server-set `received_at` + client-set `client_ts`. 8. **Privacy table**: a per-thread or per-user `telemetry_optout` flag governs ledger emission; respected at emit time. --- ## 4 open decisions for Sloba These shape Phase 1-3; please answer before dispatch: ### D1. Where does the canonical JSONL ledger live? Options: - **(A) cicd VPS** at `/var/lib/weeyuga/telemetry/` — durable, off-Mac, but requires VPS disk. ~10 MB/day at current load = ~3.6 GB/year. Recommended. - **(B) Mac local** at `~/.weeyuga/telemetry/` — fastest, but loss-on-Mac-crash, not visible to Pavilion or other agents. - **(C) Mac with hourly rsync to cicd** — best of both, more moving parts. **My recommendation: (A).** ### D2. How aggressive is content capture in JSONL / ground? - **(P0) Shape only** — token counts, model, latency, outcome, request_id. No prompt text, no response text. Privacy-preserving; fine for monetization + debugging. - **(P1) Shape + prompt** — adds the user prompt text. Useful for training-data extraction; bigger ledger. - **(P2) Shape + prompt + response** — full capture. Best for training but largest ledger and biggest privacy surface. - **(P3) Per-thread opt-in** — UI toggle \"include this thread in training data\". **My recommendation: (P0) default, (P3) toggle for thoughts on training data.** ### D3. Monetization granularity — track raw or computed? - **(M1) Just record raw token counts** — figure out pricing at query time, no per-model rate config needed. Simplest. - **(M2) Record raw + computed per-event cost in USD** — `model_pricing` table, joined at emit time. Costs change in real-time as rates change. More mid-flight work. **My recommendation: (M1) for v1. Add (M2) when we actually start charging.** ### D4. Ground integration depth — exporter vs. native emit? - **(G1) Brain emits its own format → exporter script translates to ground envelope nightly.** Decoupled, simpler to ship; minor delay before ground sees events. - **(G2) Brain emits ground envelope natively from day 1.** Tighter coupling to ground schema; gain immediate ground visibility. **My recommendation: (G2). Ground's schema is the right one; adopting it directly avoids a translation layer that drifts.** --- ## Dispatch breakdown (when greenlit) | Phase | Owner | ETA | Blocks | Blocked by | |---|---|---|---|---| | P1 plug-mobile-hole | Atlas | 1d | P2, P5 | nothing | | P2 turn-summaries + endpoints | Atlas | 2d | P5, P6 | P1 | | P3 ground envelope + JSONL | Atlas | 3d | P5, ground integration | P1, D1, D4 | | P4 multi-source ingest | Atlas + Pablo | 4d | full retrace | P3 | | P5 retrace UI | Atlas + Andre | 1w | nothing (deferrable) | P3, P4 | | P6 token-class + monetization | Atlas | 3d | nothing | P2 | | P7 retention + archival | Bane | 2d | nothing | P3 | **Critical path = P1 → P2 → P3 → P4. ~10 days.** Parallelizable side tracks: P5 (UI) and P6 (token-class) can fork after P2. --- ## What I need from Sloba 1. **Answer D1-D4** so I can dispatch with the right shape. 2. **Greenlight Phase 1 immediately** even before D2-D4 are answered — it's purely additive and unlocks everything else. 3. **Decide on the testing-mode toggle**: do you want a one-shot `WEEYUGA_TELEMETRY_VERBOSE=1` env var that turns on full content capture during your active testing windows, or always-on shape-only with explicit per-thread opt-in for content? 4. **Confirm ground priority**: should weeyuga become the 9th project in ground's portfolio graph, or do you want ground to stay AICOVENANT/TruthGraph/MemPalace-only and we have a separate weeyuga-only ledger? We accidentally shipped chat-only mobile. ## What needs to change ### Scope-block 1: `main_device_id` concept - New brain DB column / ES doc field: `users.main_device_id` (or, since we're single-user MVP, a singleton in `cluster.config` keyed `main_device_id`). - Default value: the device with most-recent heartbeat the user has actually sent a phone message to. Falls back to \"first online device in cluster.nodes\" if no history. - Mobile UI exposes it (Pablo's track) but brain-side first — desktop agent endpoint must exist before mobile can pick it. ### Scope-block 2: NEW desktop endpoint `/v1/agent/chat` - Mirrors `_handle_chat_completions` shape (multipart-or-json body with messages + model + stream) but **dispatches into `agent_service.py`'s loop**, not into Ollama proxy. - SSE stream emits: `delta` (text chunks), `tool_call_started`, `tool_call_finished`, `thinking_started`, `thinking_finished`, `model_call_started`, `model_call_finished`, `done`, `error`. - Inference inside the loop CAN route to a different node (Scope-block 4); doesn't have to stay local. - Co-located on desktop port 11435 alongside existing endpoints. - Keep `/v1/chat/completions` (bare Ollama proxy) for raw-model use cases. ### Scope-block 3: Brain dispatch routing change - `routers/mobile.py::_proxy_chat_stream` adds branch: - If `agent_loop=true` (default for phone) → dispatch to `main_device_id`'s `/v1/agent/chat` (via WS frame `{\"type\":\"agent_chat\",...}`). - If `agent_loop=false` (raw mode toggle) → existing bare Ollama path. - Default for mobile = `agent_loop=true`. - WS frame shape: `{\"type\":\"agent_chat\",\"request_id\":\"...\", \"payload\":{...}}` — symmetric to existing `chat` frame. - Brain forwards the new SSE event types unchanged to phone. ### Scope-block 4: Inference node ≠ main device - Inside agent_service.py loop, when the loop calls an LLM, the call goes through a thin \"model router\" function that picks which node has the model loaded. - Default: local node (main device's own Ollama). - Override knob: `WEEYUGA_INFERENCE_ROUTE=auto|local|<node_id>` env var. `auto` = pick by `cluster.nodes.resident_models`. - For now: just LOCAL by default. I'll dispatch him separately referencing your spec. - **Nemanja** owns the architectural spec (data model + sequence diagram + the WS frame shape). I'll dispatch him separately to write `docs/ARCHITECTURE_MOBILE_AGENT_ROUTING.md`. Don't block on him — he ratifies your shape after-the-fact. - **Mila** picks up R-AGENT-LOOP if you have research questions (\"what does Mosaic's agent_service.py loop look like exactly?\" \"are there mobile-app-routes-to-agent prior-art examples to reference?\"). She's available on demand. - **Sloba** ratifies the user-visible default: agent_loop on by default for phone (D2 in my chat with him). I'm assuming yes unless he overrides. ## Sequencing You drive this in 4 ordered phases. Each phase is independently shippable so we don't have a giant PR. | Phase | Scope | Ships | |---|---|---| | **P1** | No_think rollback (5-line patch to `_THINKING_DEFAULT_MODEL_PATTERNS`) | Tonight, immediately. Test by calling it directly with curl. | | **P3** | Brain `mobile.py::_proxy_chat_stream` switch to agent path; `main_device_id` setting; WS frame shape | This week. Phone now goes through the agent loop on the bound node. Pablo's UI work parallelizes from here. | | **P4** | Cross-node inference routing (model router function inside agent loop) | Next week. 1: """LLM routing service.
2: 
3: Exposes both a blocking `call_llm` (JSON in, JSON out) and a
4: streaming `call_llm_stream` async generator that yields tokens as
5: they arrive from the peer. The streaming path wraps Ollama's
6: OpenAI-compat `"stream": true` response and is the foundation for
7: Phase 5P.7 token streaming in the new shell.
8: 
9: 
10: Given a call request with a tier_hint and step_name, selects a peer
11: from the `llm_peers` table according to declarative rules in
12: `llm_routing_rules`, forwards the call via HTTP to the peer's
13: `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint, and emits a telemetry event.
14: 
15: Rules evaluation (Phase 2, rules-only — learned routing is future work):
16: 1. Filter rules where enabled = TRUE and tier = <tier_hint>.
17: 2. For each rule, if `step_name_pattern` is NULL, it matches any step.
18:    Otherwise the pattern is a Python regex and must re.search() match
19:    the request's step_name.
20: 3. Order matches by `priority` ASC (lower runs first); tie-break by
21:    `created_at` ASC.
22: 4. First matching rule's `peer_order` gives the sequence of peer names
23:    to try. Peers are filtered to `enabled = TRUE`; the first
24:    reachable one wins.
25: 5. If no rule matches or no peer is reachable and the rule says
26:    `fallback_to_error = TRUE`, return a routing-error telemetry.
27: 6. If no rule matches at all, use a safe default: pick the first
28:    enabled peer with tier = <tier_hint>.
29: 
30: This module does NOT stream — Phase 2.2 ships a JSON-in / JSON-out
31: router. Streaming support lands alongside the turn endpoint in a
32: later sub-phase.

358: async def _post_chat_completions_stream(

361:     """Async iterate over Ollama's OpenAI-compat streaming response.
362: 
363:     Yields dicts of the form {"content": str, "done": bool, "model": str|None}
364:     — `content` is a fresh token chunk; `done=True` marks the final
365:     frame. Raises on HTTP errors.
366:     """
367:     url = peer["base_url"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/chat/completions"
368:     model = req.model_override or peer.get("model_hint") or "default"
369: 
370:     headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
371:     if peer.get("auth_header"):
372:         name, _, value = peer["auth_header"].partition(":")
373:         if name and value:
374:             headers[name.strip()] = value.strip()
375: 
376:     body: dict[str, Any] = {
377:         "model": model,
378:         "messages": [m.model_dump() for m in req.messages],
379:         "stream": True,
380:     }
381:     if req.max_tokens is not None:
382:         body["max_tokens"] = req.max_tokens
383:     if req.temperature is not None:
384:         body["temperature"] = req.temperature
385: 
386:     async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(600.0, connect=5.0)) as client:
387:         async with client.stream("POST", url, json=body, headers=headers) as resp:
388:             resp.raise_for_status()
389:             async for raw_line in resp.aiter_lines():
390:                 if not raw_line:
391:                     continue
392:                 # Ollama / OpenAI SSE uses `data: <json>` lines; [DONE]
393:                 # marks the end. Strip the prefix, skip keepalives.
394:                 line = raw_line
395:                 if line.startswith("data:"):
396:                     line = line[len("data:"):].strip()
397:                 if line == "[DONE]":
398:                     yield {"content": "", "done": True, "model": model}
399:                     return
400:                 if not line:
401:                     continue
402:                 try:
403:                     frame = json.loads(line)
404:                 except json.JSONDecodeError:
405:                     continue
406:                 delta = {}
407:                 try:
408:                     delta = frame.get("choices", [{}])[0].get("delta") or {}
409:                 except Exception:
410:                     pass
411:                 chunk = delta.get("content") or ""
412:                 if chunk:
413:                     yield {"content": chunk, "done": False, "model": frame.get("model") or model}

1: """CDL.1 — basic per-call routing.
2: 
3: Given a chat request `(user_id, role, model_hint, messages,
4: options, allow_paid)`, pick one of the user's reachable cluster
5: nodes and forward the call to its /v1/chat/completions.
6: 
7: MVP scope (what's HERE now):
8:   1. Query cluster.nodes for ONLINE nodes (is_online=true,
9:      last_heartbeat within stale_s seconds).
10:   2. Warm-match preference: nodes whose resident_models contains
11:      model_hint win the filter.
12:   3. User-priority tie-break: nodes.priority DESC.
13:   4. HTTP POST to the chosen node's base_url/v1/chat/completions.
14:   5. Return the response body.
15: 
16: NOT HERE (deferred to CDL.2/3/+):
17:   - Per-user owner-scoping (we return any ONLINE node, regardless
18:     of who owns it). Safe until multi-user peering lands; tightened
19:     then by filtering nodes.owner_user_id OR peer_grants allowing
20:     the caller's user_id.
21:   - Role-scoping (role_allowlist) — column exists, filter doesn't
22:     yet. Easy extension once a role vocabulary is stable.
23:   - RunPod paid fallback — `allow_paid` is accepted but ignored.
24:   - 503-reroute chain (if chosen node refuses, try the next) —
25:     today's MVP returns the first error. CDL.2 adds retry loop.
26:   - Resource-budget filtering (ram_gb / vram_gb free capacity).
27:   - Cold-start scoring (we do the binary warm/not-warm pref; no
28:     scoring, no TTFT estimate).
29: 
30: All of the above ship in follow-up commits; this module's public
31: shape won't change.
32: """
33: from __future__ import annotations
34: 
35: import json
36: import logging
37: import urllib.error
38: import urllib.request
39: from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
40: from typing import Any
41: 
42: from ..db import get_pool
43: 
44: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
45: 
46: # Nodes whose last_heartbeat is older than this are considered
47: # unreachable for routing purposes (AU.1b heartbeats every 30 s).
48: DEFAULT_STALE_S = 120
49: 
50: 
51: async def candidate_nodes(
52:     *,
53:     model_hint: str | None = None,
54:     role: str = "main",
55:     stale_s: int = DEFAULT_STALE_S,
56: ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
57:     """Return a ranked list of nodes that can plausibly serve this
58:     call. Highest-ranked first. Caller walks the list in order
59:     until one succeeds."""
60:     # Hardcode channel for now; multi-channel routing is a future
61:     # extension.
62:     cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(seconds=stale_s)
63:     pool = await get_pool()
64:     async with pool.connection() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
65:         await cur.execute(
66:             """
67:             SELECT node_id, name, base_url, version_sha, channel,
68:                    is_online, is_active, resident_models,
69:                    COALESCE(priority, 0) AS priority,
70:                    last_heartbeat
71:               FROM cluster.nodes
72:              WHERE is_online = TRUE
73:                AND (last_heartbeat IS NULL OR last_heartbeat >= %s)
74:                AND base_url IS NOT NULL AND base_url <> ''
75:              ORDER BY priority DESC, last_heartbeat DESC
76:             """,
77:             (cutoff,),
78:         )
79:         rows = await cur.fetchall()
80: 
81:     cols = [
82:         "node_id", "name", "base_url", "version_sha", "channel",
83:         "is_online", "is_active", "resident_models", "priority",
84:         "last_heartbeat",
85:     ]
86:     nodes = [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in rows]
87: 
88:     # Warm-match preference. If model_hint is set AND any node has
89:     # it resident, prefer that subset.
90:     # Pablo 2026-05-06T09:15Z brain-contract bump — resident_models
91:     # is JSONB list[dict{name,engine}] now. Match against the `name`
92:     # field; flat-string entries are still tolerated for any row
93:     # that hasn't been re-heartbeat'd through the new schema yet.
94:     if model_hint:
95:         def _names(node: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
96:             ms = node.get("resident_models") or []
97:             out: list[str] = []
98:             for m in ms:
99:                 if isinstance(m, dict):
100:                     n = m.get("name")
101:                     if isinstance(n, str):
102:                         out.append(n)
103:                 elif isinstance(m, str):
104:                     out.append(m)
105:             return out
106:         warm = [n for n in nodes if model_hint in _names(n)]
107:         if warm:
108:             # Stable re-order: warm nodes first, then the rest in
109:             # priority order. The two groups keep their internal
110:             # ranking.
111:             warm_ids = {str(n["node_id"]) for n in warm}
112:             rest = [n for n in nodes if str(n["node_id"]) not in warm_ids]
113:             nodes = warm + rest
114: 
115:     return nodes
116: 
117: 
118: async def dispatch_chat(
119:     *,
120:     messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
121:     model_hint: str | None = None,
122:     role: str = "main",
123:     options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
124:     allow_paid: bool = False,
125:     timeout_s: float = 300.0,
126: ) -> dict[str, Any]:
127:     """Forward a chat request to the best available cluster node.
128: 
129:     Return shape mirrors /v1/chat/completions: OpenAI-compatible
130:     `choices[0].message.content` etc. On no-available-node returns
131:     a structured error dict the caller surfaces as HTTP 503.
132:     """
133:     nodes = await candidate_nodes(model_hint=model_hint, role=role)
134:     if not nodes:
135:         return {
136:             "error": {
137:                 "type": "no_cluster_nodes",
138:                 "message": (
139:                     "no online cluster nodes can serve this request. "
140:                     "Check /v1/cluster/nodes/status; ensure at least one "
141:                     "weeyuga serve is heartbeating within the stale window."
142:                 ),
143:             },
144:             "_dispatch": {"nodes_considered": 0},
145:         }
146: 
147:     last_error: str = ""
148:     for node in nodes:
149:         base = str(node["base_url"]).rstrip("/")
150:         if not base.endswith("/v1"):
151:             url = base + "/v1/chat/completions"
152:         else:
153:             url = base + "/chat/completions"
154: 
155:         payload: dict[str, Any] = {
156:             "model": model_hint or "",
157:             "messages": messages,
158:             "stream": False,
159:         }
160:         if options:
161:             payload["options"] = options
162:         # Ollama-compat fields mirrored verbatim.
163:         for k in ("temperature", "top_p", "max_tokens"):
164:             if options and k in options:
165:                 payload[k] = options[k]
166: 
167:         body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
168:         req = urllib.request.Request(
169:             url,
170:             data=body,
171:             headers={
172:                 "Content-Type": "application/json",
173:                 "User-Agent": "weeyuga-dispatch/1.0",
174:             },
175:             method="POST",
176:         )
177:         if model_hint:
178:             _ms = node.get("resident_models") or []
179:             _resident_names = [
180:                 (m.get("name") if isinstance(m, dict) else str(m)) for m in _ms
181:             ]
182:             warm_str = str(model_hint in _resident_names)
183:         else:
184:             warm_str = "n/a"
185:         logger.info(
186:             "dispatch: → %s (node=%s, warm=%s)",
187:             url, node.get("name"), warm_str,
188:         )
189:         try:
190:             with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_s) as r:
191:                 raw = r.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
192:                 resp = json.loads(raw)
193:                 resp["_dispatch"] = {
194:                     "node_id": str(node["node_id"]),
195:                     "node_name": node.get("name"),
196:                     "base_url": base,
197:                     "nodes_considered": len(nodes),
198:                 }
199:                 return resp
200:         except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
201:             err_body = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if exc.fp else ""
202:             last_error = f"HTTP {exc.code} from {node.get('name')}: {err_body[:400]}"
203:             logger.warning("dispatch: %s", last_error)
204:             # CDL.2: loop to next candidate on 503; today we just try
205:             # next on any error.
206:             continue
207:         except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
208:             last_error = f"{node.get('name')}: {exc}"
209:             logger.warning("dispatch: %s", last_error)
210:             continue
211: 
212:     return {
213:         "error": {
214:             "type": "all_candidates_failed",
215:             "message": f"tried {len(nodes)} node(s); last error: {last_error}",
216:         },
217:         "_dispatch": {"nodes_considered": len(nodes)},
218:     }

361:     """Async iterate over Ollama's OpenAI-compat streaming response.
362: 
363:     Yields dicts of the form {"content": str, "done": bool, "model": str|None}
364:     — `content` is a fresh token chunk; `done=True` marks the final
365:     frame. Raises on HTTP errors.
366:     """
367:     url = peer["base_url"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/chat/completions"
368:     model = req.model_override or peer.get("model_hint") or "default"
369: 
370:     headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
371:     if peer.get("auth_header"):
372:         name, _, value = peer["auth_header"].partition(":")
373:         if name and value:
374:             headers[name.strip()] = value.strip()
375: 
376:     body: dict[str, Any] = {
377:         "model": model,
378:         "messages": [m.model_dump() for m in req.messages],
379:         "stream": True,
380:     }
381:     if req.max_tokens is not None:
382:         body["max_tokens"] = req.max_tokens
383:     if req.temperature is not None:
384:         body["temperature"] = req.temperature
385: 
386:     async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(600.0, connect=5.0)) as client:
387:         async with client.stream("POST", url, json=body, headers=headers) as resp:
388:             resp.raise_for_status()
389:             async for raw_line in resp.aiter_lines():
390:                 if not raw_line:
391:                     continue
392:                 # Ollama / OpenAI SSE uses `data: <json>` lines; [DONE]
393:                 # marks the end. Strip the prefix, skip keepalives.
394:                 line = raw_line
395:                 if line.startswith("data:"):
396:                     line = line[len("data:"):].strip()

1: """CDL.1 — basic per-call routing.
2: 
3: Given a chat request `(user_id, role, model_hint, messages,
4: options, allow_paid)`, pick one of the user's reachable cluster
5: nodes and forward the call to its /v1/chat/completions.
6: 
7: MVP scope (what's HERE now):
8:   1. Query cluster.nodes for ONLINE nodes (is_online=true,
9:      last_heartbeat within stale_s seconds).
10:   2. Warm-match preference: nodes whose resident_models contains
11:      model_hint win the filter.
12:   3. User-priority tie-break: nodes.priority DESC.
13:   4. HTTP POST to the chosen node's base_url/v1/chat/completions.
14:   5. Return the response body.
15: 
16: NOT HERE (deferred to CDL.2/3/+):
17:   - Per-user owner-scoping (we return any ONLINE node, regardless
18:     of who owns it). Safe until multi-user peering lands; tightened
19:     then by filtering nodes.owner_user_id OR peer_grants allowing
20:     the caller's user_id.
21:   - Role-scoping (role_allowlist) — column exists, filter doesn't
22:     yet. Easy extension once a role vocabulary is stable.
23:   - RunPod paid fallback — `allow_paid` is accepted but ignored.
24:   - 503-reroute chain (if chosen node refuses, try the next) —
25:     today's MVP returns the first error. CDL.2 adds retry loop.
26:   - Resource-budget filtering (ram_gb / vram_gb free capacity).
27:   - Cold-start scoring (we do the binary warm/not-warm pref; no
28:     scoring, no TTFT estimate).
29: 
30: All of the above ship in follow-up commits; this module's public
31: shape won't change.
32: """
33: from __future__ import annotations
34: 
35: import json
36: import logging
37: import urllib.error
38: import urllib.request
39: from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
40: from typing import Any
41: 
42: from ..db import get_pool
43: 
44: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
45: 
46: # Nodes whose last_heartbeat is older than this are considered
47: # unreachable for routing purposes (AU.1b heartbeats every 30 s).
48: DEFAULT_STALE_S = 120
49: 
50: 
51: async def candidate_nodes(
52:     *,
53:     model_hint: str | None = None,
54:     role: str = "main",
55:     stale_s: int = DEFAULT_STALE_S,
56: ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
57:     """Return a ranked list of nodes that can plausibly serve this
58:     call. Highest-ranked first. Caller walks the list in order
59:     until one succeeds."""
60:     # Hardcode channel for now; multi-channel routing is a future
61:     # extension.
62:     cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(seconds=stale_s)
63:     pool = await get_pool()
64:     async with pool.connection() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
65:         await cur.execute(
66:             """
67:             SELECT node_id, name, base_url, version_sha, channel,
68:                    is_online, is_active, resident_models,
69:                    COALESCE(priority, 0) AS priority,
70:                    last_heartbeat
71:               FROM cluster.nodes
72:              WHERE is_online = TRUE
73:                AND (last_heartbeat IS NULL OR last_heartbeat >= %s)
74:                AND base_url IS NOT NULL AND base_url <> ''
75:              ORDER BY priority DESC, last_heartbeat DESC
76:             """,
77:             (cutoff,),
78:         )
79:         rows = await cur.fetchall()
80: 
81:     cols = [
82:         "node_id", "name", "base_url", "version_sha", "channel",
83:         "is_online", "is_active", "resident_models", "priority",
84:         "last_heartbeat",
85:     ]
86:     nodes = [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in rows]
87: 
88:     # Warm-match preference. If model_hint is set AND any node has
89:     # it resident, prefer that subset.
90:     # Pablo 2026-05-06T09:15Z brain-contract bump — resident_models
91:     # is JSONB list[dict{name,engine}] now. Match against the `name`
92:     # field; flat-string entries are still tolerated for any row
93:     # that hasn't been re-heartbeat'd through the new schema yet.
94:     if model_hint:
95:         def _names(node: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
96:             ms = node.get("resident_models") or []
97:             out: list[str] = []
98:             for m in ms:
99:                 if isinstance(m, dict):
100:                     n = m.get("name")
101:                     if isinstance(n, str):
102:                         out.append(n)
103:                 elif isinstance(m, str):
104:                     out.append(m)
105:             return out
106:         warm = [n for n in nodes if model_hint in _names(n)]
107:         if warm:
108:             # Stable re-order: warm nodes first, then the rest in
109:             # priority order. The two groups keep their internal
110:             # ranking.
111:             warm_ids = {str(n["node_id"]) for n in warm}
112:             rest = [n for n in nodes if str(n["node_id"]) not in warm_ids]
113:             nodes = warm + rest
114: 
115:     return nodes

118: async def dispatch_chat(
119:     *,
120:     messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
121:     model_hint: str | None = None,
122:     role: str = "main",
123:     options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
124:     allow_paid: bool = False,
125:     timeout_s: float = 300.0,
126: ) -> dict[str, Any]:
127:     """Forward a chat request to the best available cluster node.
128: 
129:     Return shape mirrors /v1/chat/completions: OpenAI-compatible
130:     `choices[0].message.content` etc. On no-available-node returns
131:     a structured error dict the caller surfaces as HTTP 503.
132:     """
133:     nodes = await candidate_nodes(model_hint=model_hint, role=role)
134:     if not nodes:
135:         return {
136:             "error": {
137:                 "type": "no_cluster_nodes",
138:                 "message": (
139:                     "no online cluster nodes can serve this request. "
140:                     "Check /v1/cluster/nodes/status; ensure at least one "
141:                     "weeyuga serve is heartbeating within the stale window."
142:                 ),
143:             },
144:             "_dispatch": {"nodes_considered": 0},
145:         }
146: 
147:     last_error: str = ""
148:     for node in nodes:
149:         base = str(node["base_url"]).rstrip("/")
150:         if not base.endswith("/v1"):
151:             url = base + "/v1/chat/completions"
152:         else:
153:             url = base + "/chat/completions"
154: 
155:         payload: dict[str, Any] = {
156:             "model": model_hint or "",
157:             "messages": messages,
158:             "stream": False,
159:         }
160:         if options:
161:             payload["options"] = options
162:         # Ollama-compat fields mirrored verbatim.
163:         for k in ("temperature", "top_p", "max_tokens"):
164:             if options and k in options:
165:                 payload[k] = options[k]
166: 
167:         body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
168:         req = urllib.request.Request(
169:             url,
170:             data=body,
171:             headers={
172:                 "Content-Type": "application/json",
173:                 "User-Agent": "weeyuga-dispatch/1.0",
174:             },
175:             method="POST",
176:         )
177:         if model_hint:
178:             _ms = node.get("resident_models") or []
179:             _resident_names = [
180:                 (m.get("name") if isinstance(m, dict) else str(m)) for m in _ms
181:             ]
182:             warm_str = str(model_hint in _resident_names)
183:         else:
184:             warm_str = "n/a"
185:         logger.info(
186:             "dispatch: → %s (node=%s, warm=%s)",
187:             url, node.get("name"), warm_str,
188:         )
189:         try:
190:             with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_s) as r:
191:                 raw = r.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
192:                 resp = json.loads(raw)
193:                 resp["_dispatch"] = {
194:                     "node_id": str(node["node_id"]),
195:                     "node_name": node.get("name"),
196:                     "base_url": base,
197:                     "nodes_considered": len(nodes),
198:                 }
199:                 return resp
200:         except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
201:             err_body = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if exc.fp else ""
202:             last_error = f"HTTP {exc.code} from {node.get('name')}: {err_body[:400]}"
203:             logger.warning("dispatch: %s", last_error)
204:             # CDL.2: loop to next candidate on 503; today we just try
205:             # next on any error.
206:             continue
207:         except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
208:             last_error = f"{node.get('name')}: {exc}"
209:             logger.warning("dispatch: %s", last_error)
210:             continue
211: 
212:     return {
213:         "error": {
214:             "type": "all_candidates_failed",
215:             "message": f"tried {len(nodes)} node(s); last error: {last_error}",
216:         },
217:         "_dispatch": {"nodes_considered": len(nodes)},
218:     }
"}}

986:     def _handle_chat_no_think_via_native(self, req: dict, raw: bytes) -> None:
987:         """Reroute a non-streaming /v1/chat/completions request through
988:         Ollama's native /api/chat with think:false, reshape the native
989:         response to OpenAI-compat. Triggered for thinking-default
990:         families to prevent <think> drain.
991: 
992:         On any HTTP 400 from /api/chat (which can happen if Ollama is
993:         old enough that it rejects the `think` body field), fall through
994:         to the standard OpenAI-compat proxy with the original body so
995:         callers still get *something* back.
996:         """
997:         import time as _t
998: 
999:         server: _DeviceServer = self.server  # type: ignore[assignment]
1000:         ollama_root = server.upstream
1001:         if ollama_root.endswith("/v1"):
1002:             ollama_root = ollama_root[:-3]
1003:         ollama_root = ollama_root.rstrip("/")
1004: 
1005:         # Translate OpenAI-compat fields → Ollama native body
1006:         options: dict[str, Any] = {}
1007:         if isinstance(req.get("max_tokens"), (int, float)):
1008:             options["num_predict"] = int(req["max_tokens"])
1009:         if isinstance(req.get("temperature"), (int, float)):
1010:             options["temperature"] = float(req["temperature"])
1011:         if isinstance(req.get("top_p"), (int, float)):
1012:             options["top_p"] = float(req["top_p"])
1013:         if isinstance(req.get("seed"), int):
1014:             options["seed"] = int(req["seed"])
1015:         body: dict[str, Any] = {
1016:             "model": req.get("model"),
1017:             "messages": req.get("messages") or [],
1018:             "stream": False,
1019:             "think": False,
1020:         }
1021:         if options:
1022:             body["options"] = options
1023:         if req.get("keep_alive") is not None:
1024:             body["keep_alive"] = req["keep_alive"]
1025: 
1026:         data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
1027:         rq = urllib.request.Request(
1028:             ollama_root + "/api/chat",
1029:             data=data,
1030:             method="POST",
1031:             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
1032:         )
1033:         try:
1034:             with urllib.request.urlopen(rq, timeout=600) as r:
1035:                 resp_raw = r.read()
1036:         except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
1037:             if e.code == 400:
1038:                 # Old Ollama that doesn't know `think` — fall through
1039:                 # to the OpenAI-compat path with the original body.
1040:                 return self._proxy("POST", "/chat/completions", body_override=raw)
1041:             err = e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:400]
1042:             return self._send_json(e.code, {"error": f"upstream HTTP {e.code}: {err}"})
1043:         except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
1044:             return self._send_json(502, {"error": f"upstream: {e}"})
1045: 
1046:         try:
1047:             doc = json.loads(resp_raw)
1048:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
1049:             return self._send_json(502, {"error": "ollama returned non-JSON"})
1050: 
1051:         # Reshape native /api/chat → OpenAI /v1/chat/completions
1052:         msg = doc.get("message") or {}
1053:         content = (msg.get("content") or "").strip()
1054:         done_reason = doc.get("done_reason") or ("stop" if doc.get("done") else "length")
1055:         # OpenAI-compat finish_reason set: stop | length | content_filter | tool_calls
1056:         finish_reason = "stop" if done_reason == "stop" else "length" if done_reason == "length" else done_reason
1057: 
1058:         prompt_tokens = int(doc.get("prompt_eval_count") or 0)
1059:         completion_tokens = int(doc.get("eval_count") or 0)
1060: 
1061:         out = {
1062:             "id": f"weeyuga-nothink-{int(_t.time())}",
1063:             "object": "chat.completion",
1064:             "created": int(_t.time()),
1065:             "model": doc.get("model") or req.get("model"),
1066:             "choices": [{
1067:                 "index": 0,
1068:                 "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": content},
1069:                 "finish_reason": finish_reason,
1070:             }],
1071:             "usage": {
1072:                 "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens,
1073:                 "completion_tokens": completion_tokens,
1074:                 "total_tokens": prompt_tokens + completion_tokens,
1075:             },
1076:             "_weeyuga_meta": {
1077:                 "thinking_bypass": "auto",
1078:                 "via": "ollama:/api/chat (think=false)",
1079:             },
1080:         }
1081:         return self._send_json(200, out)

194:     # failover, not a long hang on TCP setup.

210:     """Pull (content, model, input_tokens, output_tokens) from an
211:     OpenAI-compat /v1/chat/completions response.
212: 
213:     Qwen3 family models in thinking mode put their answer in
214:     `message.reasoning` rather than `message.content`. When content is
215:     empty, fall back to reasoning so callers see SOMETHING — otherwise
216:     a thinking-mode reply silently looks like "model returned nothing".
217: 
218:     Tool-calls (when present) are NOT folded into `content` here —
219:     callers that care use `call_llm()` and read the `raw` field on
220:     the response. This function stays content-only for the existing
221:     callers that don't know about tools.
222:     """
223:     content = ""
224:     try:
225:         msg = data["choices"][0]["message"] or {}
226:         content = msg.get("content") or ""
227:         if not content:
228:             # Two field names appear in the wild:
229:             #   - `reasoning` — Qwen3 thinking-mode (Ollama)
230:             #   - `reasoning_content` — gemma / llamacpp builds

132: def record_agent_event(
133:     event_type: str,
134:     payload: dict[str, Any],
135:     context: dict[str, Any] | None,
136: ) -> None:
137:     """Best-effort local telemetry append.
138: 
139:     This must never break the agent loop. All exceptions are swallowed
140:     after a timestamped terminal notice.
141:     """
142:     ts = utc_now_iso()
143:     ctx = dict(context or {})
144:     node_id = ctx.get("node_id") or _read_node_id()
145:     record = {
146:         "ts": ts,
147:         "event_type": event_type,
148:         "thread_id": ctx.get("thread_id"),
149:         "turn_id": ctx.get("turn_id"),
150:         "relay_request_id": ctx.get("relay_request_id"),
151:         "request_id": ctx.get("request_id"),

155:         "inference_node_id": ctx.get("inference_node_id"),
156:         "model_id": ctx.get("model_id"),
157:         "model_invocation_name": ctx.get("model_invocation_name"),
158:         "transport": ctx.get("transport"),
159:         "payload": summarize_payload(event_type, payload),
160:     }
161:     try:
162:         path = _log_path(ts)
163:         path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
164:         with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
165:             fh.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
166:     except Exception as exc:

404: def _tier_from_model(model: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
405:     """Best-effort map model-name → (tier, reason).
406: 
407:     Returns one of `fast`/`standard`/`coder`/`thinking`. Reason is a
408:     short string for the `reason` envelope field so an operator
409:     grepping ELK can see *why* the tier came out the way it did.
410: 
411:     Order matters — coder + thinking markers win over size markers,
412:     because a `qwen2.5-coder:0.5b` is still a coder model even if
413:     it's small.
414:     """
415:     if not model:
416:         return ("standard", "model_empty:default_standard")
417:     m = model.lower()
418:     # Coder family wins regardless of size.
419:     if "coder" in m:
420:         return ("coder", "model_pattern:coder")
421:     # Thinking / reasoning models — DeepSeek R1, OpenAI-style o1,
422:     # qwq, qwen3 (thinking by default), or any explicit `:think` tag.
423:     if (
424:         ":think" in m
425:         or "qwq" in m
426:         or "deepseek-r1" in m
427:         or m.startswith("r1")
428:         or m.startswith("o1")
429:         or m.startswith("qwen3:")
430:     ):
431:         return ("thinking", "model_pattern:thinking")
432:     # Small models go to fast tier.
433:     for marker in _TIER_FAST_SIZE_MARKERS:
434:         if marker in m:
435:             return ("fast", f"model_pattern:size_small{marker}")
436:     return ("standard", "model_pattern:default_standard")
